discovery: Phase-sensitive Josephson-interference determination of d-wave pairing symmetry in high-temperature cuprate superconductors

nominees.name: Chang C. Tsuei
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center (emeritus), USA

motivation: Spectroscopic probes measure only the magnitude of the gap. Unconventional superconductivity, though, is defined by the sign of the order parameter. Van Harlingen's corner-SQUID experiments (1993) and Tsuei and Kirtley's tricrystal-ring experiments (1994 onward) used Josephson interference to detect that sign directly. Their observation of spontaneously generated half-flux quanta and pi-phase shifts showed beyond doubt that cuprate pairing has d(x2-y2) symmetry. These results settled the central controversy of high-Tc superconductivity. They also founded phase-sensitive junction physics: pi-junctions, the zero-bias Andreev bound states seen in tunnelling, and today's interface-based searches for spin-triplet, odd-frequency and topological pairing all rest on the principle they established. Pi-junctions are now used in superconducting circuits as well. The work is a model of decisive experiments that turned a symmetry question into a direct measurement and remains the benchmark for identifying unconventional superconductors.
